breakpoints.note: The PoC passes the harness size check (28 bytes is within 10-5120) and is admitted into the SHORT_TERM credential branch of stun_check_message_integrity_str, where the strncpy type confusion corrupts len.

First project-code statement that parses the attacker-controlled STUN buffer, searching for a MESSAGE_INTEGRITY attribute using the corrupted buffer length. The attribute at offset 20 (type 0x0008, length 20) is found because the corrupted len makes the bounds check in stun_get_command_message_len_str vacuously pass.

strncpy returns char * (the destination pointer pwd), but its return value is implicitly converted to size_t and assigned to len. This overwrites the caller-supplied buffer length with a stack address, corrupting len from its actual value (28) to a huge number (~0x7fff...).

memcmp reads 20 bytes starting at old_hmac (buf + 24). The actual buffer is only 28 bytes, so the last 16 bytes of the 20-byte read extend into adjacent uninitialized heap memory, triggering MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value.
